operationName: Ebola PHEIC Response — 2026 Bundibugyo Outbreak, DRC & Uganda
heroHeadline: June 4 Situation Report: DRC Ebola Outbreak — Ituri Province Response Coordination Ongoing
heroSubtitle: By 2 June 2026, the 2026 DRC-Uganda Bundibugyo virus (BDBV) outbreak reached 336 total lab-confirmed cases — DRC: 321 (299 Ituri across 15 health zones, 19 Nord-Kivu across 7 health zones, 3 Sud-Kivu) plus Uganda: 15 confirmed — with 49 confirmed deaths (48 DRC, 1 Uganda). The most significant development on June 2 was the confirmation of local transmission chains within Uganda: 7 of the 15 Uganda cases are now attributed to within-country secondary spread rather than direct DRC travel, with 8 cases in Kampala. DRC confirmed cases surged by 39 in 24 hours as mobile BSL-3 lab throughput continued converting suspected to confirmed status, while suspected DRC cases fell to 116 (from 220+) reflecting accelerated throughput. MSF is constructing a 65-bed ETC in Mongbwalu — the outbreak's most volatile cluster zone — alongside the Goma 80-bed ETC (operational June 1) and ETCs under construction in Bukavu and Lwiro. No licensed BDBV vaccine or therapeutic is available. The 4-week Uganda-DRC border closure entered its sixth day.
footerNote: Data sourced from WHO Disease Outbreak News (DON602–DON605), DRC Ministry of Health (MSANTE), Uganda Ministry of Health, CDC Ebola Situation Summary, ECDC, MSF, NBC News, and ReliefWeb. Case counts are rapidly evolving.
